title: Regularity and bounds for repeated interval averaging
statement:
Let $\eta>0$, let $c\ge0$, and let $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be $c$-Lipschitz. For each natural number $m$, set $\phi=S_\eta^{m+1}\psi$, the result of applying the translated interval average $m+1$ times. Then $\phi$ is $m+1$ times continuously differentiable and $c$-Lipschitz, and for every $x\in\mathbb R$,
\[|\phi(x)-\psi(x)|\le(m+1)c\eta,\qquad |\phi^{(m+1)}(x)|\le c(2/\eta)^m.\]
replaced: For $\eta>0$ and a real function $\psi$, write $S_\eta\psi(x)=\eta^{-1}\int_0^\eta\psi(x+t)\,dt$. If $\psi$ is $c$-Lipschitz with $c\ge0$ and $m\ge0$ is an integer, put $\phi=S_\eta^{m+1}\psi$, where the exponent denotes repeated application of $S_\eta$. Then $\phi$ is $C^{m+1}$ and $c$-Lipschitz, and for every real $x$, $|\phi(x)-\psi(x)|\le(m+1)c\eta$ and $|\phi^{(m+1)}(x)|\le c(2/\eta)^m$.
